question.problem:
In a cafe, there is a kettle and a microwave oven. The random variable $X$ represents the number of breakdowns per year of the kettle, and the random variable $Y$ is the number of breakdowns per year of the microwave oven. The probability distributions of $X$ and $Y$ are given below.
$x$ $0$ $1$ $2$ $3$
$f(x)$ $0.2$ $0.4$ $0.3$ $0.1$
$y$ $0$ $1$ $2$
$f(y)$ $0.6$ $0.3$ $0.1$

Calculate the expected number of breakdowns per year of both appliances.
question.worked_solution:
We need to calculate $\text{E}[X+Y].$

Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are random variables (not necessarily independent), and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

$$
\text{E}[aX+bY]=a\text{E}[X]+b\text{E}[Y].
$$

The expected values of $X$ and $Y$ are calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =0\cdot 0.2+1\cdot 0.4+2\cdot 0.3+3\cdot 0.1=1.3 \\ \text{E}[Y] & =0\cdot 0.6+1\cdot 0.3+2\cdot 0.1=0.5\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we get

$$
\text{E}[X+Y]=\text{E}[X]+\text{E}[Y]=1.3+0.5=1.8.
$$
